title: B. Following Directions
statement:
Alperen is standing at the point (0,0). He is given a string s of length n and performs n moves. The i-th move is as follows:

The first line of the input contains an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 1000) — the number of testcases.

The first line of each test case contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 50) — the length of the string.

The second line of each test case contains a string s of length n consisting of characters textttL, textttR, textttD, and textttU, denoting the moves Alperen makes.

For each test case, output "YES" (without quotes) if Alperen passes the candy, and "NO" (without quotes) otherwise.

You can output the answer in any case (for example, the strings "yEs", "yes", "Yes" and "YES" will be recognized as a positive answer).

In the first test case, Alperen follows the path (0,0) oversettextttU→ (0,1) oversettextttU→ (0,2) oversettextttU→ (0,3) oversettextttR→ (1,3) oversettextttD→ (1,2) oversettextttD→ colorgreen(1,1) oversettextttL→ (0,1). Note that Alperen doesn't need to end at the candy's location of (1,1), he just needs to pass it at some point.

In the second test case, Alperen follows the path (0,0) oversettextttU→ (0,1) oversettextttR→ colorgreen(1,1).

In the third test case, Alperen follows the path (0,0) oversettextttR→ (1,0) oversettextttR→ (2,0) oversettextttR→ (3,0) oversettextttU→ (3,1) oversettextttU→ (3,2) oversettextttD→ (3,1) oversettextttD→ (3,0) oversettextttD→ (3,-1).

In the fourth test case, Alperen follows the path (0,0) oversettextttL→ (-1,0) oversettextttL→ (-2,0) oversettextttL→ (-3,0).

Input:
```
77UUURDDL2UR8RRRUUDDD3LLL4DUUR5RUDLL11LLLLDDRUDRD
```

Output:
```
YES
YES
NO
NO
YES
YES
NO
```
